Automatic forecasts from reporting history

First review and calculate reports in the converter above. This tool matches account balances across reporting dates and learns a forecast from their history. Reports must use consistent accounting policies, currency and account identities.

Matching and data issues
AccountLatest signed balanceFinal forecast signed balanceModelSelection MAELatest holdout error
Positive balances are debit-side; negative balances are credit-side. Overall totals sum the comparable accounts only. Missing accounts are excluded, never assumed to be zero. These account-balance forecasts are not cash-flow forecasts or a balanced future financial statement. Short histories use a clearly labelled repeat-last baseline. The tool does not estimate prediction intervals or model seasonal/accounting changes.
Your financial data
Sample data loaded — these figures are fictional, not your financial records.
Upload a trial balance with Code, Description, Debit, Credit columns, or a table with Month, Income, Expenses columns for one or more reporting periods, or Date, Income, Expenses for at least 30 consecutive days. Revenue / inflows and costs / outflows headers also work. Word files must be .docx; PDFs must contain selectable text. Scanned PDFs and old .doc files need conversion first.
Match your report’s columns
Choose the header row and layout. Line-item reports let you identify income and expense rows; balance reports use debit and credit columns. Review the imported values before forecasting.
Choose each row’s role. Rows set to Ignore are excluded; exclude subtotal and total rows to avoid counting them twice.

Account balance scenario
This workbook supplies one reporting date. Choose daily or monthly steps and enter an assumed change per step to project a selected account balance. This is an assumption-based scenario, not a learned trend or a cash-flow forecast. It does not produce a balanced future trial balance.

Signed balances use debit minus credit. Negative credits remain negative. Empty debit/credit cells are treated as zero. Select one source worksheet at a time; duplicate worksheets are not added together.

Models are selected separately for income and expenses using rolling one-period-ahead mean absolute error (MAE). Future values are constrained to zero or above. Scenario adjustments apply to every forecast period; they are not compounded growth. Long-range accuracy has not been validated.
